rationale: CR-001 (major, patch): the ptPreset.ts token swap in commit 1bc4cdcda that fixed the pure-black selected item replaced it with bg-surface-interactive-active (#1A1A1A dark), which computes to ~1.09:1 contrast against the panel bg-surface-base-secondary (#212224 dark) -- far below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 minimum, and the same near-invisible pairing already documented as a contrast failure for this exact token in EPMCDME-8547; a purpose-built higher-contrast token (bg-surface-specific-dropdown-focused, #888888 dark) already exists in this codebase for this exact case. The acceptance lens file predates this commit and still cites the superseded bg-surface-base-navigation token, so AC1/AC2 were re-graded directly against current source instead of trusted as-is, which caps confidence at low; AC4 independently stays partial on the unenforced options referential-stability invariant. 1 finding deferred as pre-existing (provider/static-type id collision in DataSourceTypeSelector's un-deduplicated options merge, out of this styling fix's scope) and 1 dismissed as noise (the referential-stability edge case, reconfirmed unreachable -- all current Autocomplete call sites are referentially stable per the prior review round's exhaustive check, and this round's diff does not touch option-passing logic).

findings.title: Selected item background fails contrast in dark theme
findings.problem: The selected-item token was swapped from bg-surface-base-navigation (pure black, #000000 dark) to bg-surface-interactive-active, which resolves to neutral['925'] = #1A1A1A in dark theme, rendered inside the Autocomplete panel whose background (bg-surface-base-secondary) is neutral['875'] = #212224.
findings.impact: The computed contrast ratio between #1A1A1A and #212224 is ~1.09:1, far below the WCAG 1.4.11 non-text-contrast minimum of 3:1 -- the same token pairing already measured and documented as a contrast failure (~1.1:1) for the sibling Dropdown/MultiSelect focus state in EPMCDME-8547. The selected item is now visually almost indistinguishable from the panel background in dark theme, so while the literal pure-black glitch is gone, the selected-state affordance itself is effectively invisible.
findings.recommendation: Use a token proven to meet 3:1 against the dark panel background, e.g. bg-surface-specific-dropdown-focused (neutral['525'] = #888888 dark), which EPMCDME-8547 already introduced for exactly this class of dropdown-item contrast problem in the sibling Dropdown/MultiSelect presets, and verify the resulting ratio against #212224 in both themes.
